text:
beth: heads up — getting a bunch of customer reports of 502/504 from hosted inference starting ~09:12 UTC. errors spike on model routes that rely on prefix cache.

jordan: oncall looking now, seeing memcached errors in the metrics. p95 latency for cache GET jumped from 4ms -> 120ms and ttfb for gateway increased.

mike: customers reporting timeouts in the api with `error: upstream cache timeout` in their app logs. one customer included a curl repro.

ashley: can you paste the gateway logs / cache logs? curious if this is auth-related or connection saturation.

beth: pasting clipped logs below — trimmed to noisy lines

```
2026-03-16T09:12:31Z gateway-1 ERROR route=get-model err="cache_get: i/o timeout" route_id=client-abc model=redwood-3b
2026-03-16T09:12:32Z memcached-7 WARN conn=10.0.2.14 op=get key_prefix=usr:kvs: shard=12 err="connect timeout"
2026-03-16T09:12:33Z gateway-1 WARN fallback_to_origin route=get-model duration_ms=1200
2026-03-16T09:12:34Z runtime-3 ERROR kv_prefetch worker=45 err="prefix fetch: incomplete response"
```

beth: sample curl customer repro (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \
  -H 'OpenAI-Organization: cust-123' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"hi"}' -v
```

jordan: seeing memcached cluster node 7 flapping, leader-election events in cluster logs around the same time. suspect partial partition + connection pool exhaustion.

infra-bot: [alert] memcached-cluster shard-12 high-error-rate 09:11:50 -> 09:18:00, error-type: CONNECT_TIMEOUT, affected-pods: memcached-7, memcached-9

ashley: quick triage notes:
- gateway has aggressive cache timeouts (200ms) for prefix reads to keep llm latency tight. when memcached latencies spike we hit circuit-breaker -> gateway returns 502/504.
- we have fallback-to-origin but origin is also under strain due to thundering cache fill.

mike: customers want an ETA — any quick mitigations?

jordan: immediate mitigations in progress:
- scale memcached replicas + increase connection pool to gateway (hotfix rolling).
- temporarily increase cache read timeout to 500ms for affected routes (to reduce immediate 502s).
- enable circuit-breaker backoff so fallback doesn't flood origin.

beth: rolled the timeout increase to 10% of traffic on canary at 09:22. telemetry shows decrease in 502 rate for that canary.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: memcached-scaleup v1.2.3 -> starting canary 09:24 UTC

ashley: follow-ups to investigate root cause:
- check memcached eviction/oom logs and kernel drops on nodes 7/9.
- look at network errors between gateway and cache (tcp_retransmits, conn reset).
- inspect prefix-sharding heuristics — one shard saw 6x request concentration (hotkey?)

jordan: repro steps for eng to reproduce locally:
1) run a traffic replay that hits same prefix pattern (headers: X-Customer-ID=cust-123).
2) throttle memcached node egress (tc qdisc netem delay 100ms loss 1%).
3) observe gateway circuit-breaker -> 502, and origin thundering on fills.

mike: I've told the customer we're investigating, applied canary mitigation, and will follow up in 30m.

beth: assigning postmortem owner: @ashley. please include timeline, root cause (leader-election + hotspot + aggressive timeouts), and hardening items: connection pool tuning, progressive cache timeout backoff, shard rebalancer alert, and synthetic monitoring for prefix latency.

ashley: noted. will kick off PM and add runbook updates for "cache prefix latency spike".

jordan: marking incident status -> mitigated at 09:40 UTC (502 rate returned to baseline after scale+timeout). will keep monitoring. :white_check_mark:

mike: thanks all, I'll update customer with mitigation and next steps. :pray:

beth: closing thread once postmortem PR is merged.
